PullRequest.Title: sessions: close side pane on last tab close when multiple chats are shown
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

In the Agents window with the per-chat layout (`sessions.experimental.layoutScope: "chat"`), closing the last editor tab while more than one chat of the same session is shown (for example a split chat group, or a subagent chat next to the main chat) left the side pane open with only the empty group's Add Tab actions. You then had to press **Close Editor Area** separately.

This regressed in #341141. That PR switched the last-editor-close guards from "multiple **sessions** visible" to `_multipleLayoutOwnersVisible()`, which in the `chat` scope means "multiple **chats** shown". Chats of the same session share that session's main editor part, so a second chat of the same session has no reason to keep an empty side pane open.

**Change:** both last-editor-close guards (`DesktopExistingSessionStrategy._registerEmptyGroupClose` and `DesktopDraftSessionStrategy._registerLastEditorClose`) check `multipleSessionsVisibleObs` again. The per-chat ownership introduced in #341141 is unchanged everywhere else (restore, capture, detail sync). Keeping the side pane open when several **sessions** are visible stays intentional and is still covered by the existing test.

**How to test**
1. Set `"sessions.experimental.layoutScope": "chat"` and reload the Agents window.
2. Open a session that has two chats, then run **Agents: Split Chat Group Right** so both chats are shown.
3. Open Changes (`Ctrl+Shift+G`) and close the Changes tab.
4. Before this change, the side pane stays open with the empty group's Add Tab actions. After it, the side pane closes and the chats take the full width.

**Validation**
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/desktopStrategies.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/desktopLayoutController.test.ts --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/test/browser/chatLayoutOwnership.test.ts`: 235 passing. The new Existing Session multi-chat test failed before the fix and passes after it.
- `npm run typecheck-client`: passed.
- `npm run eslint` and hygiene on the changed files: passed.
- Live run of the Agents window from sources using the steps above: reproduced before the fix (side pane stayed open) and confirmed after it (side pane closes).

Scenarios.Scenario: Close the last editor in an existing session while multiple chats from that same session are shown, or while another mounted session is hidden
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor-close event synchronously reads the active session, cached visibility observables, and main-part emptiness; the changed guard then permits hideSidePane(), which serially hides the editor and auxiliary bar before the close handling completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: JSON.stringify a fixed-size part-visibility object and call storageService.store while hiding each visible part
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most two fixed-size serializations/store calls for the one last-editor close (one for editor visibility and one for auxiliary-bar visibility); zero for non-last closes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The previous multiple-layout-owner guard returned early in these chat-layout configurations, so the side pane was not hidden and these visibility stores were not performed by this close event.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The small serialization/store calls occur synchronously during the newly permitted pane hide; any backing flush behavior is outside the reviewed code, and payload size is constant.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One predicate evaluation per editor-close event; pane hiding occurs only when the main editor part becomes empty. Observable reads and persisted visibility payload are constant-size regardless of chat/session count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Fully synchronous and serialized on the UI event path; no spawned tasks, queues, fan-out, or concurrent boundary calls.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: multipleSessionsVisibleObs and multipleChatsVisibleObs are derived observables, so reads use current derived state; no cold/warm remote cache behavior or misses. The visibility state persisted after each changed part is a fixed four-field object.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard, event path, two part-visibility updates, and fixed-size persistence are directly traced. There is no collection-scaled or repeated expensive work.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual DOM/grid relayout and storage backend duration vary by platform, but work is bounded to one final-close transition and fixed-size state.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff intentionally performs one bounded pane-collapse transition that was previously skipped; the constant observable checks and at-most-two tiny persistence operations do not create realistic scaling, throughput, or latency risk.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close the last editor for a draft/Quick Chat under per-chat layout with multiple same-session chats or only hidden additional sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: onDidCloseEditor synchronously validates the main group and session state, reads the cached visibility predicates, clears two pending keys, and calls hideSidePane(); editor and auxiliary-bar hiding complete on the event path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist fixed-size editor/auxiliary-bar visibility state through storageService.store during hideSidePane
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or two fixed-size stores on the final close depending on which side-pane parts were visible; no store from this path on earlier closes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old guard skipped hideSidePane when multiple chat layout owners were visible, so this close event did not persist the hidden part state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs during the final-close UI transition, but remains fixed and bounded; no per-chat or per-session fan-out occurs.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One evaluation per closed editor, with pane work only when all main-part groups are empty. Cost does not grow with the number of chats, sessions, editors already closed, or session lifetime.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single synchronous event handler; editor and auxiliary-bar transitions are sequential and no asynchronous or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Visibility predicates are cached derived observables; there is no external cache lookup or negative-cache behavior. Visibility persistence is fixed-size and only occurs for parts whose state changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: direct call flow shows one bounded hide and constant-size persistence, with no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network calls found.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Layout complexity can affect the one-time hide cost, but the diff does not multiply it by chat/session cardinality or event history.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The newly reached synchronous UI work is the intended final-close behavior and is bounded to one transition, while avoiding continued rendering of the empty side pane afterward.

Scenarios.Scenario: Close editors while multiple distinct sessions are actually shown, or close a non-last editor in any layout
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The close handler evaluates _otherSessionShown and the existing empty-main-part checks, then returns without toggling the side pane when another session is shown or content remains.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One or two cached boolean observable reads per close plus existing constant-time/session-state checks; no iteration over visible sessions or chats is added.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous predicate evaluation only; no work is queued and no external operations are started.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Both visibility values come from derived observables whose underlying derivations are length/count comparisons; cold and warm behavior are equivalent for this constant-size read, with no remote cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the helper short-circuits and never enumerates the visible collections.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: None material: the changed incremental cost is at most one additional cached boolean read when multiple sessions are present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No regression. Behavior remains an early return for genuinely multi-session layouts, and the added check is constant-time with no boundary, allocation, or layout work.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all four changed files and traced both last-editor-close paths through pane layout and visibility persistence. The diff adds only cached boolean checks and, in the newly corrected cases, one bounded side-pane hide with fixed-size persistence. No actionable diff-introduced performance regression or qualifying performance-regression fix was found.
